Bug_Title: MC: An overridable method is called from the clone() method. (MC_OVERRIDABLE_METHOD_CALL_IN_CLONE)
Bug_Details:
Calling overridable methods from the clone() method is insecure because a subclass could override the method,
affecting the behavior of clone(). It can also observe or modify the clone object in a partially initialized
state. Only static, final or private methods should be invoked from the clone() method. 
See SEI CERT rule
MET06-J. Do not invoke overridable methods in clone().
Bug_Explanation: The clone() method in the CloneBugExample class calls the overridable method setData(), which could be overridden by a subclass. This can lead to unexpected behavior if a subclass modifies the method or observes changes during cloning.
Trigger_Explanation: The testShowBug method invokes the showBug method, which triggers the bug when calling the clone method. The clone method calls the overridable method setData, leading to potential unexpected behavior due to the overridable method being invoked in a partially initialized state.
